description:

additional_info.subject: 0421900 - ID0421739 -DC/Si-D/FI-[MP / P6 170000741]-Duplicated OCPP StartTransaction for one session [C1] CRM:00314000166
additional_info.body:
Hi Markus,
I am reaching out in regards of ticket
ID0421900,
opened for charger
YX5xq0,
which on 29.04.2025 experienced #16 sessions which had the OCPP StartTransaction command duplicated.
I had an overview on AWS if this behavior happened other times, and I confirm it happened only on 29.04.2025. In the last 2 weeks (30.04 - 14.05) and in the 2 weeks before the event, it never happened.
I analyzed the logs, and these are my findings:
In correlation to the duplicated StartTransaction message, I see duplicated “secc events” coming from the sicharge-cp-backend.
The two StartTransaction messages have two different TransactionIDs
Not only the StartTransaction message is duplicated, but also the MeterValues messages are duplicated. In this case, they both refer to a single TransactionID.
The StopTransaction message is instead unique, not duplicated.
In #11 cases, the charging session was stopped immediately.
In #5 duplicated cases, the charging session was possible, and the pattern was the following:
OCPP: Received result: StartTransaction (transactionID:
A
)
OCPP: Received result: StartTransaction (transactionID:
B
)
OCPP: Send command: MeterValues (transactionID:
B
)
OCPP: Send command: StartTransatcion (transactionID:
B
)
At 2025-04-29T14:38:44 a reboot was performed.
After the reboot, the charger received all the 16 StopTransaction messages that were sent as duplicated. You can verify that in the excel sheet attached.
Can you please let me know what were the messages seen from OCPP Backend side? Did they see a duplication of messages?
I suspect a temporary issue on the communication between EcoG and FW, since a reboot cleared the situation and all the StopTransaction messages of the duplicated sessions were sent afterwards.
At the same time, this behavior happened only in a single day over the past month, so if it was a bug I would expect to see it more often, but I would rather consider it as a single event of failure.
Thank you in advance for your feedback with the data from the Backend.
With kind regards,
